headline: Sales grow on Innovative Medicine strength; EPS holds flat
summary_short: Revenue rose 6.6% y/y to $25.3B, led by Innovative Medicine growth of 7.8% despite STELARA's biosimilar-driven decline; net income was flat at $5.53B as a $0.4B talc litigation charge offset operating gains, and diluted EPS slipped 0.9% y/y to $2.27.
summary_long: Q2 2026 worldwide sales of $25.3B grew 6.6% y/y (5.6% operational, 1.0% currency), with Innovative Medicine up 7.8% on CAPLYTA and broad-based growth offsetting a 7.6% STELARA drag from biosimilar competition; MedTech grew 4.5%. Gross margin expanded 32bp to 68.2% as operational leverage and favorable currency offset unfavorable mix and MedTech tariff costs. SG&A ticked up 60bp to 25.4% of sales on commercial investment; R&D fell 40bp to 14.4% on Innovative Medicine expense phasing. Net income was flat at $5.53B and diluted EPS slipped 0.9% to $2.27, as a $0.4B talc litigation charge (vs. none a year ago) offset the operating gain. Cash fell to $20.4B; total debt declined to $49.0B. No new company guidance was issued in the filing.

drivers.explanation: Innovative Medicine +7.8% (CAPLYTA, broad growth) and MedTech +4.5% drove sales; STELARA biosimilar erosion cut about 4.6% off worldwide operational growth.
Operational leverage and favorable currency in both segments were partially offset by unfavorable STELARA-driven mix and MedTech tariff costs.
Increase driven by commercial investments in the Innovative Medicine and MedTech businesses.
Decrease driven by expense phasing in Innovative Medicine, partially offset by higher Surgery and Cardiovascular investment in MedTech.
A $0.4B talc litigation charge this quarter, versus none a year ago, offset growth in operating income and held net income flat y/y.
Tracks flat net income; a slightly higher weighted diluted share count versus prior year left diluted EPS down y/y.
Six-month comparisons are distorted by a $7.0B talc reserve reversal booked in Q1 2025; Q2-only results are cleaner but still carry a new $0.4B talc charge.

confidence_notes: FORCED REGENERATION — this summary supersedes and overwrites a prior kpi-only summary for the same period, upgraded here to filing depth by reading the SEC 10-Q. No forward guidance was disclosed in the 10-Q body (JNJ issues guidance separately via investor materials, not the 10-Q).
